standard: FAIAS - Financial AI Independent Assurance Standard
derived_copy: This file is a derived copy made from the signed FAIAS text. The signed text is each file at its `url`, and its sha256 is in the signed manifest.
signature_statements: A signature shows that a file has not changed since the owner signed it. It says nothing about whether the text is correct, or about a firm that uses FAIAS.
A reader that did not calculate the sha256 of a file has not verified that file. It can state only which version and manifest root the file names.

The public key is in the same repository as the text. So a check with that key shows only that the files agree with each other. A comparison of the key with a copy held elsewhere, for example in the Zenodo record, shows that it is the owner's key.

summary.text: FAIAS is a baseline for reviewing generative, agentic and predictive AI systems in financial institutions.

limits.text: FAIAS is not a certification or approval scheme: no one is authorised to certify, accredit or approve anything against it.
The reviewer never tests production systems
★1 is a statement about the field, never a reason to skip.
The ★ rating in each canvas carries its anchor inside the rating artefact
integrity — the content has not changed since signing — and authorship control
The signature binds content to a key, not to a moment in time.
An opinion at any tier is given at limited assurance.

records.question: Is the quantity the model is trained or configured to predict or optimise a valid proxy for the substantive construct the decision is actually about — and has proxy validity been tested at subgroup level, including for cases where the historical label itself encodes prior unequal treatment rather than the true outcome of interest?

records.subdomain: E.6 Control Efficacy Under Adversarial Evolution
records.question: Where an AI system functions as a control — fraud detection, AML/transaction monitoring, surveillance, screening or promotion approval — has its detection rate and residual miss rate been measured against adversarially evolved inputs, mapped to a recognised adversarial-ML taxonomy, rather than only against historical or static case libraries; and is control efficacy re-tested on a defined cadence as adversary technique evolves?
